---

### Step 1: Silent Uninstall Command (Inno Setup / Standard Executable)
Most MiniTool applications are packaged using Inno Setup. Their native uninstallers support standard silent switches. 

Open an elevated **PowerShell** or **Command Prompt** (Run as Administrator) and run[1]:

```cmd
"%ProgramFiles%\MiniTool Partition Wizard\unins000.exe" /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART
```

*(Note: Adjust the path if your installation resides in `C:\Program Files (x86)` or a custom directory. If you are targeting **Power Data Recovery** or **System Booster**, replace the folder name accordingly).*

---### Step 2: PowerShell Script for Total Leftover Removal
After the silent uninstaller executes, residual directories, cache data, scheduled tasks, and registry configurations usually remain. Run the following comprehensive **PowerShell script (as Administrator)** to scrub them completely:

```powershell
# ==========================================
# MiniTool Complete Leftover Removal Script
# ==========================================

Write-Host "Stopping any lingering MiniTool processes..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
Stop-Process -Name "*MiniTool*" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

Write-Host "Removing Program Files directories..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
$PathsToRemove = @(
    "$env:ProgramFiles\MiniTool*",
    "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\MiniTool*",
    "$env:ProgramData\MiniTool*",
    "$env:ProgramData\Partition Wizard*",
    "$env:Public\Desktop\MiniTool*"
)

foreach ($path in $PathsToRemove) {
    if (Test-Path $path) {
        Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $path -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        Write-Host "Deleted: $path" -ForegroundColor Green
    }
}

Write-Host "Clearing User AppData profiles..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
# This scans all user profiles for leftover local/roaming cache and configurations
Get-ChildItem -Path "C:\Users\" -Directory | ForEach-Object {
    $userAppDataLocal = Join-Path $_.FullName "AppData\Local\MiniTool*"
    $userAppDataRoaming = Join-Path $_.FullName "AppData\Roaming\MiniTool*"
    
    Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $userAppDataLocal -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $userAppDataRoaming -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

Write-Host "Cleaning up orphaned Scheduled Tasks..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object { $_.TaskName -like "*MiniTool*" } | Unregister-ScheduledTask -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

Write-Host "Scrubbing Registry Leftovers..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
$RegPaths = @(
    "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\MiniTool",
    "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\MiniTool",
    "HKCU:\SOFTWARE\MiniTool",
    "HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Partition Wizard"
)

foreach ($reg in $RegPaths) {
    if (Test-Path $reg) {
        Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $reg -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        Write-Host "Removed Registry Key: $reg" -ForegroundColor Green
    }
}

# Clean installer artifacts from Installer registry hives
Get-ChildItem "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall", "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | 
    Where-Object { $_.GetValue("DisplayName") -like "*MiniTool*" } | 
    ForEach-Object {
        Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $_.PSPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        Write-Host "Removed Uninstall registry entry: $($_.PSPath)" -ForegroundColor Green
    }

Write-Host "MiniTool complete cleanup finished. A system reboot is recommended." -ForegroundColor Yellow
```

2. **Delete stuck driver services:**

